questions.q: What does the summary say happened to Frank Abagnale's shortcuts?
a: They became his whole way of life
They stopped working after one year
They landed him a legitimate job
They were taught to him by his father
questions.why: Lesson 1 explains that what began as a means to impress women turned into an end in itself.

questions.q: Why does the summary say lying is harder than telling the truth?
a: You must keep track of every lie you have told
People rarely believe a stranger's lies
Lies require expensive costumes and props
The law punishes lies more severely
questions.why: Lesson 2 points out that the truth stays the same for years, while a growing web of lies must be maintained.

questions.q: What did Frank keep in his notebook to sustain his pilot act?
a: Airline jargon, names, and details of people he met
A list of banks he planned to target
Contacts for buying fake passports
Records from his father's business
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes notes on insider phrases, technical data and profiles so real crews would not see through him.

questions.q: What happened to Frank after he was captured?
a: He was paroled to help the FBI with fraud cases
He served the full twelve-year sentence
He fled the country and disappeared
He became a commercial airline pilot
questions.why: Lesson 3 says he spent only five years in jail and was released early in exchange for helping the FBI.

questions.q: What lesson does the summary draw from Frank's later career?
a: A skill you dismiss may later prove useful
Crime never pays in the end
Always finish your formal education
Forgiveness matters more than justice
questions.why: Lesson 3 shows him building a long career helping banks spot forged checks, using what he once did wrong.
